title: Stored physical sample may disclose sensitive personal or health information
description: A physical sample placed into freezer storage can itself reveal sensitive information about an identifiable person, including genetic, biomarker, or disease-related characteristics, if someone with access can inspect, test, or otherwise derive information from it beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: The sample is linkable to a participant directly or via labels, codes, or accompanying records, and storage personnel or other parties may gain physical or procedural access.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure from data at rest in a datastore; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode wording for physical sample storage may vary.

title: Stored sample and labels may enable linkage to an individual across systems or studies
description: Labels, barcodes, freezer location metadata, or coded identifiers attached to the physical sample can allow the stored sample to be linked back to a specific participant or correlated with records in other repositories, increasing re-identification risk.
assumptions: The sample container or storage records contain persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or study codes that can be correlated with other information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability via identifiers/metadata on stored items; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Sample storage may make the data subject identifiable
description: Even if pseudonymous, a physical sample in storage may remain identifiable because DNA or other unique biological characteristics, together with labels or associated storage records, can identify the data subject.
assumptions: The sample contains unique biological material or is accompanied by identifiers or metadata sufficient for re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate for identifiability of stored data objects; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Stored physical sample may be used for purposes beyond the subject's expectations or consent
description: Once the sample is stored, it may later be retrieved, tested, or shared for secondary research, operational, or commercial purposes that are not transparent to the data subject, causing unawareness about ongoing and future processing.
assumptions: Participants are not continuously informed about all subsequent storage, access, reuse, or secondary analysis activities involving the sample.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node under unawareness relating to secondary use and insufficient transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Sample retention or freezer storage may exceed consented or legally permitted conditions
description: The physical sample may be stored longer than necessary, in a location or under governance conditions not covered by consent, ethics approval, or applicable law, resulting in non-compliance with privacy and data protection obligations.
assumptions: Retention periods, storage conditions, access restrictions, cross-border issues, or purpose limitations apply to the sample.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit compliance node for unlawful/excessive retention or storage-governance mismatch; exact subnode may vary.

title: Sample may be exposed during handoff from wet lab to freezer storage
description: During transport or handoff from the wet lab to storage, the physical sample and its labels may be visible to unauthorized personnel or left unattended, disclosing participant-related information.
assumptions: The transfer involves physical movement through shared spaces or temporary staging before freezer placement.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure during transfer/in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Unauthorized correlation of de-identified sample ID with identities in LIMS
description: The LIMS stores the mapping between the de-identified sample ID and identifying context. Sending the de-identified ID back to the wet lab can enable inference of the underlying person or sample owner if the wet lab can correlate it with local records, timestamps, or prior identifiers.
assumptions: Wet Lab personnel or systems may have access to auxiliary information such as collection context, prior labels, or processing schedules.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for inference/linking at a datastore may vary.

title: Linkability of samples across wet-lab processing using persistent de-identified ID
description: A stable de-identified sample ID used by the wet lab may allow records, assay runs, or observations concerning the same sample to be linked across processing stages or datasets, even without direct identifiers.
assumptions: The de-identified ID is reused across multiple steps, systems, or exports rather than being transaction-specific.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability from reuse of a persistent pseudonymous identifier.

title: Detectability of sample presence from receipt of de-identified ID
description: Receipt of a de-identified ID by the wet lab reveals that a corresponding sample exists and is being processed. An observer of this flow or a party with access to wet-lab work queues may detect the presence of an individual's sample even if direct identity is omitted.
assumptions: An attacker can observe the flow, logs, or wet-lab task lists and has some contextual knowledge about who might have submitted samples.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id for detectability of existence/presence on this flow may differ.

title: Insufficient auditability of de-identified ID assignment and transmission
description: If the LIMS does not keep reliable audit records of when a de-identified ID was assigned and sent to the wet lab, parties may later be unable to prove who accessed, generated, or transmitted the pseudonymous sample metadata.
assumptions: Logging, integrity protection, or time-stamped audit trails may be incomplete or not regularly reviewed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation-related node id; exact subtree may differ depending on whether the focus is sending, receiving, or logging.

title: Use of de-identified sample ID beyond the stated laboratory purpose
description: The wet lab may reuse the de-identified ID for secondary purposes such as additional analyses, staff training datasets, or broader internal sharing, beyond the original purpose for which the identifier was returned, creating a policy/consent compliance risk.
assumptions: Purpose limitation or downstream-use controls are weak, ambiguous, or not technically enforced.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for non-compliance with purpose limitation/consent obligations.

title: Unprotected storage of raw sequence data may expose sensitive genetic and health-related information
description: Raw sequence data can contain uniquely identifying genetic markers and information that reveals or strongly suggests health conditions, ancestry, familial relationships, or other sensitive traits. If the cluster filesystem stores these data without strong access control or encryption, unauthorized parties may learn highly sensitive personal information from the files.
assumptions: The sequence data are human or otherwise attributable to individuals, and the cluster filesystem is accessible by multiple users, services, or administrators.

title: Stored sequence datasets may be linkable to the same individual across studies or systems
description: Even when direct identifiers are removed, genomic sequence data are often effectively unique. Storing raw sequence data in a shared cluster filesystem can allow records to be linked with other datasets, projects, or prior submissions, enabling correlation of the same person across contexts.
assumptions: The filesystem or surrounding environment permits access to multiple datasets or metadata sources that can be compared or joined.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Raw sequence files may enable singling out of an individual
description: A raw genomic sequence can act as a near-unique identifier. Once stored, a person may be singled out from a population or dataset based on distinctive genomic features, particularly if an attacker can query or inspect stored files and associated metadata.
assumptions: The sequence data concern individuals and are stored with enough fidelity and metadata to distinguish one person from others.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability/singling-out; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Storage of raw sequence data may exceed consent, purpose limitation, or retention expectations
description: Persistently storing digital raw sequence data in the cluster filesystem may be incompatible with the data subject's consent, approved study purpose, data minimization commitments, or retention limits. Privacy risk arises if the storage is broader, longer, or more reusable than originally authorized.
assumptions: Consent terms, IRB approvals, contracts, or policy constraints exist regarding purpose, duration, or scope of genomic data storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary by catalog version.

title: Individuals may be unaware that raw sequence data are being stored in a shared cluster environment
description: Data subjects may not understand that their raw sequence data are copied from the wet lab into a cluster filesystem, potentially accessible to multiple teams, administrators, backups, or downstream analysis processes. This lack of awareness reduces transparency and can undermine informed decision-making.
assumptions: The storage arrangement and downstream accessibility are not clearly communicated to data subjects or data providers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for unawareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Stored raw sequence data may become hard to delete completely from cluster storage and backups
description: Once raw sequence data are written to the cluster filesystem, copies may persist in snapshots, backups, replications, caches, or derived working areas. This can prevent timely and complete deletion when retention periods expire or erasure is requested, extending privacy exposure.
assumptions: The cluster filesystem uses replication, snapshotting, backup, or caching mechanisms typical of research compute environments.

title: Linkability of sequence datasets across compute jobs
description: Raw sequence data sent from the cluster filesystem to compute nodes may carry stable sample identifiers, file paths, metadata, or content-derived signatures that allow different processing runs or datasets to be linked to the same data subject, sample, or study across jobs.
assumptions: Sequence data and associated metadata contain persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers visible to compute jobs or operators.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability on data flows may vary.

title: Identifiability of individuals from raw sequence data on compute nodes
description: Digital raw sequence data is often inherently identifying or can become identifying when processed with metadata. Once transferred to compute nodes, users, processes, or administrators with access may be able to identify a person, donor, or sample source.
assumptions: Human or otherwise sensitive biological sequence data is included, and compute-node access is broader than strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability arising from data content on a flow/processing target.

title: Disclosure of sensitive sequence data during transfer or processing
description: Raw sequence data moved from the filesystem to compute nodes may be exposed to unauthorized parties through insecure transport, shared memory/scratch space, overly broad file permissions, job logs, or compromised compute processes.
assumptions: Transport or runtime environments may be shared or insufficiently isolated.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to disclosure threat tree; exact node for disclosure in transit vs at destination may differ.

title: Detectability of presence of a subject or study from transfer activity
description: Even if payload content is protected, the existence, timing, size, or frequency of transfers from the cluster filesystem to compute nodes can reveal that a particular subject, cohort, or study is being processed, enabling inference about participation or operational events.
assumptions: Adversaries can observe network, scheduler, storage, or job activity metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detectability often depends on observability of metadata rather than payload.

title: Processing raw sequence data beyond consent or declared purpose
description: Sequence data sent to compute nodes for transformation into objective-specific outputs may be reused for secondary analyses, model training, or broader research objectives not covered by the original consent, contract, or privacy notice.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and consent constraints exist and are not technically enforced in the compute environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance due to purpose creep/consent mismatch.

title: Insufficient transparency about use of sequence data in compute processing
description: Data subjects or data providers may be unaware that raw sequence data is transferred into distributed compute nodes, potentially copied to scratch locations, transformed through multiple pipelines, or retained in intermediate artifacts, reducing their ability to understand how data is used.
assumptions: System notices or records of processing do not fully describe internal data flows and intermediate processing.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; unawareness categorization is high-level due to limited flow context.

title: Insufficient evidence of authorized access and processing on compute nodes
description: If transfer and use of raw sequence data on compute nodes are not logged with strong attribution, actors may later deny having accessed, copied, or processed sensitive data, undermining accountability and incident investigation.
assumptions: Audit trails for data access, job execution, and dataset provenance are incomplete or weakly bound to user identities.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-repudiation/accountability threat.

title: Unnecessary exposure of research data in delivery zone
description: Moving context-relevant research data from the cluster filesystem into the Data Delivery DMZ may make the data visible to a broader set of systems, operators, or recipients than necessary for the intended delivery purpose. If full datasets or rich metadata are staged in the DMZ without minimisation, sensitive attributes may be disclosed.
assumptions: The Data Delivery DMZ is less restricted or more broadly accessible than the originating cluster filesystem, and delivered datasets may contain personal or sensitive research-related information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-fit estimate for disclosure due to oversharing/excessive visibility in a datastore-to-datastore transfer.

title: Linkability through persistent identifiers or metadata across deliveries
description: If the staged research data in the DMZ retains stable subject identifiers, file names, project IDs, pseudonyms, or consistent metadata, recipients or observers may link records belonging to the same data subject across separate deliveries or with external datasets.
assumptions: The transferred data includes direct identifiers, pseudonyms, quasi-identifiers, or stable metadata that persist into the delivery environment.
uncertainty_note: Node id is inferred as a linkability threat from retained identifiers/metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree mapping may differ.

title: Identifiability of data subjects in delivered research data
description: Context-relevant research data sent to the DMZ may contain direct identifiers or combinations of quasi-identifiers that allow recipients or DMZ users to identify individual data subjects, especially once prepared for external delivery.
assumptions: The dataset contains personal data or can become identifying when combined with other available information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from dataset contents; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Inference of sensitive information from staged dataset and metadata
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, the combination of variables, filenames, folder structure, timestamps, cohort descriptions, or delivery metadata in the DMZ may enable inference of sensitive facts about individuals or groups.
assumptions: Attackers or recipients can access auxiliary information or observe delivery-related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit estimate for detectability/disclosure by inference; exact subtree node may differ.

title: Processing in the DMZ beyond the original consent or legal basis
description: Copying research data into the delivery DMZ for distribution may constitute additional processing, disclosure, or cross-boundary transfer that is not fully covered by the original participant consent, data-use agreement, or other legal basis unless explicitly governed.
assumptions: The data is personal data subject to purpose limitation, sharing restrictions, or participant consent constraints.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with consent/legal basis due to transfer and delivery staging.

title: Retention in the delivery environment beyond necessity
description: Datasets staged in the Data Delivery DMZ may remain stored longer than necessary after delivery, conflicting with storage limitation obligations and increasing privacy risk through prolonged availability.
assumptions: No automatic deletion or retention control is enforced in the DMZ.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for retention/storage-limitation non-compliance; exact numbering may vary.

title: Insufficient proof of authorised transfer from source datastore
description: If the cluster filesystem does not maintain auditable records of who initiated the transfer, what dataset version was sent, and under which approval, it may be impossible to prove or dispute whether a specific disclosure to the DMZ was authorised.
assumptions: Transfer logging, approval linkage, or provenance controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit estimate for non-repudiation gap around transfer provenance; exact node id may differ.

title: Recipients may be unaware that their data is staged for external delivery
description: Data subjects may not be sufficiently informed that their research data is copied from internal storage into a delivery DMZ and made available for downstream sharing, reducing transparency about processing locations and disclosures.
assumptions: Notices to data subjects do not explicitly describe staging in a DMZ or external delivery workflow.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness often depends on organisational transparency obligations rather than a purely technical property; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Requester identity exposed through sample request records
description: The physical sample request sent by the NCCoE Researcher to the DNA Store may contain direct identifiers of the requester, such as name, employee identity, email, or organizational role. If request records are broadly accessible or insufficiently protected, parties with access to the DNA Store or request logs could learn who is requesting which physical sample.
assumptions: The request includes researcher identity or contact details and is stored or logged by the DNA Store.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of identity in the request context; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Sensitive request contents disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The sample request may reveal sensitive content such as requested specimen identifiers, associated study context, disease area, or intended sequencing activity. Disclosure of this information from the DNA Store, request queue, or transmission path could expose sensitive personal or research-related information linked to the requested sample.
assumptions: The request references specific samples or metadata that are sensitive and the request is retained or transmitted in readable form.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure of data/content rather than identity.

title: Researcher activity can be inferred from sample request submission
description: Observing that a particular researcher submitted a physical sample request to the DNA Store may allow an observer to infer involvement in a specific project, study phase, disease domain, or sequencing operation. Even without reading full contents, timing and destination of the request can reveal private information about researcher actions and research focus.
assumptions: An observer can monitor request events, metadata, or access logs.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node selection for inference from observable request metadata.

title: Sample request enables linkage between researcher and specific biological sample
description: The request may create or expose a link between the NCCoE Researcher and a specific physical sample or donor-related record. If the DNA Store maintains request histories, an attacker or insider could correlate requestor identity with sample identifiers and other datasets, increasing re-identification or profiling risk.
assumptions: The request includes persistent sample identifiers and requester identity, and these can be correlated with other records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability created by associating requester and sample identifiers.

title: Researcher may later deny having requested the physical sample
description: If the request process lacks strong authentication, integrity protection, or auditable proof of submission, the NCCoE Researcher could deny making the request, or the DNA Store could be unable to prove which individual initiated it. This weakens accountability for access to physical samples that may be privacy-sensitive.
assumptions: Request submission may not be strongly bound to the requester through non-repudiable evidence.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for lack of evidence enabling repudiation/deniability.

title: Data subject or sample provenance may be unaware of this access request
description: Submitting a physical sample request to the DNA Store may trigger sample retrieval and downstream sequencing preparation without the underlying data subject, donor, or sample provenance authority being aware that this specific physical sample is being requested for a new use. This can reduce transparency around sample handling and access.
assumptions: The process does not automatically notify donors, custodians, or relevant oversight actors of each request.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is inferred from the described process; exact affected party and subtree may vary.

title: Physical sample request may exceed consent or approved processing scope
description: The requested physical sample may be used for sequencing or research purposes not fully covered by the donor's consent, ethics approval, or data-use restrictions. If the DNA Store accepts and processes such a request without checking purpose, authorization, or consent constraints, the flow can result in non-compliant handling of personal biological material.
assumptions: Consent, ethics, or policy restrictions exist for at least some samples and are not perfectly enforced at request time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance due to missing policy/consent enforcement; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Unnecessary exposure of specimen-associated information during retrieval
description: When the DNA Store releases a physical sample to the NCCoE Researcher, labels, chain-of-custody paperwork, or accompanying request details may reveal more information about the donor or case than is necessary for the research task, increasing identifiability.
assumptions: Physical samples or accompanying documentation contain identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or metadata beyond a minimal pickup token.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; I am using a generic identifiability/disclosure-style node because exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labels may vary.

title: Linkability of repeated sample retrievals by the same researcher or for the same donor
description: Repeated retrieval events can allow observers at the DNA Store or in surrounding processes to link multiple sample pickups to the same researcher, project, or underlying donor, enabling profiling of research activity or donor participation.
assumptions: Retrieval events are logged or observable and use stable identifiers such as researcher identity, request id, specimen id, or donor-related labels.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ; this is intended as a generic linkability node.

title: Researcher can infer donor identity from the physical sample or packaging
description: The physical sample itself, its packaging, or attached documentation may contain direct identifiers or rich contextual metadata that allows the NCCoE Researcher to determine the identity of the data subject behind the specimen.
assumptions: The sample or packaging includes names, medical record numbers, collection dates, location, or other identifying context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort disclosure/discoverability-style node selection; exact node naming in LINDDUN Pro may vary.

title: Store can detect sensitive researcher interest through retrieval requests
description: By observing which specimens are requested and retrieved, the DNA Store can detect sensitive attributes about the NCCoE Researcher's projects or infer sensitive characteristics of the involved donors, such as disease focus, ancestry, or participation in a specific study.
assumptions: Specimen identifiers or request context are semantically meaningful or can be mapped to sensitive categories.
uncertainty_note: I am less certain of the exact detectability node id here; conceptually this is detectability of sensitive interest through the retrieval flow.

title: Insufficient proof of handoff or receipt of the physical sample
description: If the transfer from the DNA Store to the NCCoE Researcher is not strongly recorded, either party may later dispute whether a specific physical sample was released, received, or released in the proper condition, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant handling.
assumptions: Handoff logging, signatures, tamper evidence, or witness controls may be weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: Generic non-repudiation node used; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree identifier may differ.

title: Retrieval and release may exceed consent or approved purpose
description: A physical sample may be retrieved by the NCCoE Researcher for a purpose, study, or retention period not covered by the donor's consent, ethics approval, or data-use restrictions, creating a policy and legal non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Use restrictions exist and are not automatically enforced at sample release time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Donor is insufficiently informed about physical sample retrieval and downstream use
description: The retrieval process may not be transparent to the donor, leaving the individual unaware that the sample has been accessed by a researcher, for what purpose, and under what safeguards, which undermines intervenability and transparency expectations.
assumptions: There is no subject-facing notification, audit access, or transparent disclosure mechanism for sample access events.
uncertainty_note: I am using a generic unawareness/intervenability-related node; exact LINDDUN Pro labeling may differ.

title: Unnecessary identity disclosure when receiving the physical sample
description: The receiving clerk may learn the identity of the NCCoE researcher or directly identifying details attached to the sample or shipping paperwork, even if the clerk only needs a specimen identifier and handling instructions to route the sample for sequencing.
assumptions: The package, chain-of-custody form, or sample label may include researcher name, contact details, organization, or other direct identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct disclosure of identity to an unintended or unnecessary recipient on this flow.

title: Linkability of the physical sample to other submissions or records
description: Consistent sample identifiers, shipment metadata, packaging characteristics, or accompanying paperwork could allow the receiving clerk or others handling intake to link this physical sample to prior or future submissions from the same researcher or study.
assumptions: The same identifiers, sender details, courier account data, or study codes are reused across shipments.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability through shared identifiers or metadata on a physical transfer.

title: Identifiability of the researcher or associated data subject from shipment metadata
description: Even if the sample itself is pseudonymous, labels, return address information, chain-of-custody forms, or study context may make the NCCoE researcher or the associated participant/data subject identifiable to the receiving clerk.
assumptions: The shipment contains identifiers or quasi-identifiers sufficient to single out a person or organization contact.
uncertainty_note: Applies if identifying or quasi-identifying metadata accompanies the specimen; node id chosen as a best-fit for identifiability.

title: Information disclosure through mishandling, loss, or tampering of the physical sample in transit or intake
description: If the physical sample or accompanying paperwork is intercepted, misdelivered, opened, or left accessible during handoff to the receiving clerk, sensitive context about the sample, researcher, or associated participant may be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: There is some sensitive information on the specimen container, packaging, or accompanying documentation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-fit estimate for unauthorized disclosure arising during transport/receipt of a physical item rather than a digital channel.

title: Lack of proof or disputability of sample handoff
description: If receipt of the physical sample is not logged with time, sender, condition, and recipient, either party may later be unable to prove that the sample was sent, received, or received in a specific condition, affecting accountability for privacy-relevant handling.
assumptions: Chain-of-custody controls may be informal or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation issues around physical handoff and receipt.

title: Collection of excessive personal information during sample intake
description: The intake process may request or retain more personal information than is necessary for sequencing and routing, such as full researcher details or participant-related context beyond what is needed to process the sample.
assumptions: The lab's intake forms or procedures may not be data-minimized.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with data minimization/purpose limitation obligations during collection.

title: Exposure of sensitive test intent on the request form
description: The physical test request form handed to the patient may reveal sensitive health information, the purpose of genetic testing, clinician identity, or specimen details to anyone who sees it while the patient carries or stores it.
assumptions: The form contains personal identifiers and/or clinically sensitive testing information rather than being fully pseudonymous.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via data in transit/physical handover; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Linkability of patient identity to genetic sample request
description: The request form can directly associate the patient's identity with a specific genetic test or forthcoming biological sample, enabling linkability between the person, the sample, and the sequencing workflow if the form is observed or copied.
assumptions: The form includes direct identifiers and a unique request/reference number used later in the lab process.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through identifiers on the form; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Identifiability of the patient from the request paperwork
description: Even if the sample itself might later be pseudonymized, the request paperwork given to the patient may contain name, date of birth, address, medical record number, or clinician details that make the patient directly identifiable.
assumptions: The request form contains explicit identifiers or a combination of quasi-identifiers sufficient to identify the patient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for direct identifiability from provided data; exact node id may vary.

title: Patient may lack proof of what request information was provided
description: If the handover is informal and not acknowledged, the patient may later be unable to prove what sample request, instructions, or disclosures were actually provided, while the clinician may also be unable to prove receipt by the patient.
assumptions: The handover may occur without signed acknowledgment, copy retention, or audit trail.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is a weaker fit here than disclosure/identifiability because the flow is a physical handover; node id is approximate.

title: Insufficient transparency about downstream use of the sample request and specimen
description: The patient may not fully understand from the form alone how the sample and associated data will be used, shared with the sequencing lab, retained, or linked to results, reducing awareness of privacy consequences.
assumptions: The request form or accompanying explanation may be incomplete or hard to understand.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Collection and sharing fields on the request form may exceed what is necessary
description: The clinician may provide a form that requests more personal, familial, or clinical information than is necessary for obtaining and routing the physical sample, creating risk of non-compliance with data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: The form template may include broad clinical history or identifiers not strictly necessary for this stage of the process.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to excessive data collection/disclosure; exact subnode may differ.

title: Clinician can infer sensitive patient health information from the physical sample
description: A physical sample itself can reveal special-category personal data such as genetic, diagnostic, infectious disease, toxicology, reproductive, or substance-use information. Simply retrieving or viewing the sample may disclose more information than is necessary for the immediate care task.
assumptions: The sample or accompanying physical identifiers/labels expose patient identity and/or sensitive attributes to the clinician beyond strict need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; I am using a generic detectability/disclosure node because exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming for physical sample exposure may vary.

title: Patient identity may be linkable to the retrieved physical sample
description: If the sample container or request carries direct identifiers or stable codes, the clinician can associate the sample with a specific patient identity. This may enable identification of the patient from the sample even where pseudonymous handling would otherwise be possible.
assumptions: The sample request or label includes patient name, MRN, barcode, or other linkable identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro identification subnode may differ.

title: Physical sample can be linked with other patient records or encounters
description: The retrieved sample and its request metadata may contain identifiers, timestamps, specimen numbers, or context that allow the clinician or others to link this sample to other records, visits, or systems, increasing the patient's traceability across contexts.
assumptions: There are shared identifiers or correlatable metadata across sample handling and clinical record systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic linkability node; exact subnode is uncertain.

title: Retrieval or secondary use of the physical sample may exceed patient consent or legal basis
description: The clinician's retrieval of the physical sample may not align with the patient's consent, purpose limitation, or other legal basis if the sample is accessed for a broader or different purpose than originally communicated or authorized.
assumptions: Consent and purpose constraints exist for the sample, and the retrieval context could diverge from them.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro consent/compliance subnode is uncertain.

title: Patient may be unaware that the clinician retrieves and uses the physical sample
description: The handling of the physical sample may not be transparent to the patient, especially if the retrieval occurs later or by a different clinician than the one who originally requested or collected it. This can undermine the patient's awareness of who accessed the sample and for what purpose.
assumptions: The process does not clearly notify the patient about subsequent retrieval/access events.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort unawareness node; exact subnode is uncertain.

description: If physical handoff or pickup of the sample is not logged with time, actor, and purpose, the clinician or organization may later be unable to prove who retrieved the sample or whether retrieval was authorized. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant access.
assumptions: Physical sample retrieval may occur outside strong custody-chain logging or acknowledgment controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-repudiation node; exact subnode is uncertain.

title: Unnecessary exposure of patient-identifying information on the physical sample
description: The physical sample or its packaging may carry direct or indirect identifiers (e.g., patient name, MRN, date of birth, clinic labels) that are not strictly necessary for the receiving clerk to process intake, disclosing more personal data than needed during transport and receipt.
assumptions: Assumes the sample container, requisition, or shipment materials include identifiers beyond a minimal study/sample code.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label for data minimization/excessive disclosure may differ.

title: Linkability of the physical sample to the patient's identity across contexts
description: Consistent identifiers on the sample, shipping paperwork, or lab accessioning records can allow the receiving clerk or downstream lab staff to link the specimen to the same individual across clinical and research contexts, increasing the ability to build a broader profile of the person.
