title: LIMS can link de-identified sample IDs back to individuals via retained metadata
description: Although the flow creates a de-identified ID, the metadata stored in LIMS may still contain quasi-identifiers, timestamps, project context, operator information, or cross-system references that allow records to be linked to a specific person or participant when combined with other datasets.
assumptions: LIMS stores sample metadata together with the generated de-identified ID and has access to other contextual fields or external mappings.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability through stored records; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: Stored sample metadata may enable re-identification despite use of a de-identified ID
description: If the metadata accompanying the generated sample ID includes direct or indirect identifiers, an internal user or connected system may infer the data subject's identity from the supposedly de-identified record.
assumptions: Sample metadata in LIMS includes enough attributes to single out or reconnect a sample to a person.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from stored data; exact subnode may differ.

title: LIMS storage of generated sample IDs may expose existence of an individual's sample
description: Even if identity is not directly known, the presence of a de-identified sample record in LIMS may allow an observer with auxiliary knowledge to detect that a given person participated in a study, submitted a sample, or is associated with a particular workflow or condition.
assumptions: An attacker or insider can query, observe, or correlate LIMS records with outside knowledge such as collection dates or study enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/exposure of record existence; exact LINDDUN Pro node label may differ.

title: Generation of de-identified IDs may be inconsistent with consent or stated processing purpose
description: The Wet Lab may generate and send de-identified sample identifiers to LIMS for reuse, tracking, or secondary processing beyond what the data subject consented to or what was originally declared, creating a policy/compliance privacy risk.
assumptions: Consent or notice may limit downstream storage, reuse, or linkage of sample metadata.
uncertainty_note: This depends strongly on governance context not present in the DFD; node id is a best-fit estimate for non-compliance with consent/purpose constraints.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that de-identified IDs still permit downstream tracking in LIMS
description: The act of generating a de-identified sample ID may create an impression of anonymity, while in practice the identifier can still support longitudinal tracking, internal correlation, or future relinking within LIMS or connected systems, reducing transparency to the data subject.
assumptions: Users or participants are told samples are de-identified without a clear explanation of residual linkage and traceability risks.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is inferred from the flow semantics rather than explicit notice artifacts; exact subnode may differ.

title: Unauthorized recipient can infer sensitive attributes from delivered research data
description: Making context-relevant research data available in the DMZ for retrieval may expose personal or sensitive attributes to a party beyond the intended need-to-know if access controls are weak, credentials are shared, or dataset scope exceeds what is necessary. Even a trusted recipient may learn more about data subjects than intended from direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or rich contextual content.
assumptions: The research data may contain personal data, pseudonymous data, or high-dimensional records that remain inferable to individuals; retrieval is performed over a network-accessible DMZ repository.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit generic detectability/disclosure-style node for data being made available to a recipient; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Linkability across delivered datasets or prior disclosures
description: The recipient may be able to link records in the delivered dataset with other datasets already held by the recipient or third parties, enabling correlation of the same individual across contexts. Repeated deliveries through the DMZ can also preserve stable identifiers, timestamps, or unique combinations of attributes that facilitate linkage.
assumptions: Delivered data contains stable identifiers, pseudonyms, metadata, or quasi-identifiers that can be correlated across releases or with external data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from data content/metadata; exact node mapping may vary.

title: Identifiability of data subjects by the trusted recipient
description: Even if the data is intended to be context-relevant only, the trusted recipient may be able to identify individual data subjects from direct identifiers, rare attribute combinations, embedded metadata, or auxiliary information available to the recipient.
assumptions: The recipient has some auxiliary knowledge or can access external datasets that increase re-identification risk.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability due to dataset contents and recipient-side auxiliary knowledge; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure from overbroad data publication in the DMZ
description: The DMZ may expose more research data than is necessary for the recipient's purpose, such as full datasets instead of filtered subsets, inclusion of unnecessary fields, or retention of files for longer than needed. This increases the amount of personal information disclosed during retrieval.
assumptions: Data minimization, purpose limitation, field-level filtering, or lifecycle controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Chosen as a best-fit disclosure-of-information/data disclosure node for overbroad availability; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient consent, purpose, or legal-basis alignment for recipient retrieval
description: Making the research data available to the NCCoE-trusted recipient may be incompatible with the original consent, notice, data-sharing agreement, or other legal basis under which the data was collected. Even if technically authorized, the transfer/retrieval could exceed the stated research context or subject expectations.
assumptions: Use restrictions, participant consent terms, DUAs, or policy constraints may apply to onward sharing to this recipient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for unlawful or policy-misaligned sharing; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of what data was retrieved and by whom
description: If retrieval from the DMZ is not strongly logged and attributable, the sender may be unable to prove which recipient account accessed which dataset version and when, and the recipient may later dispute retrieval or scope. This undermines accountability for privacy-relevant disclosures.
assumptions: Audit logging, immutable access records, and recipient authentication may be incomplete or not strongly bound to an individual operator.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-repudiation node for disputed retrieval/access events; exact node id may differ.

title: Recipients may be unaware of data handling constraints or subject expectations
description: The retrieval mechanism may not clearly communicate retention limits, onward-sharing restrictions, de-identification caveats, or research-use boundaries. As a result, recipient operators may process the data in ways that data subjects would not expect or that exceed agreed handling constraints.
assumptions: Policy notices, machine-readable usage controls, or dataset labeling may be limited or absent in the DMZ delivery process.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node for insufficient transparency/communication of data handling constraints; exact node id may differ.

title: Unauthorized recipient retrieves context-relevant research data from the DMZ
description: If access control on the Data Delivery DMZ is weak or misconfigured, an unintended party could retrieve the context-relevant research data, disclosing personal or sensitive research data to unauthorized recipients.
assumptions: The DMZ hosts retrievable data and is reachable by the Trusted Research Data Recipient over a network boundary; access control and recipient authentication are relied upon to limit retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for unauthorized access/disclosure from a datastore-to-external-entity retrieval flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Delivery endpoint enables linkability of recipient access sessions
description: Repeated retrievals from the same DMZ endpoint may allow logs, identifiers, network metadata, or stable download tokens to be correlated over time, linking multiple access sessions to the same recipient or research project.
assumptions: The delivery mechanism produces server, network, or application logs containing stable identifiers, IP addresses, account names, or token values.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for linkability through shared identifiers/metadata in access events.

title: Recipient access patterns reveal the existence or nature of a research subject or dataset
description: The act of retrieving specific context-relevant research data may reveal information about the recipient's study focus, cohort, or the existence of particular data subjects or sensitive categories, even without reading the full content.
assumptions: Observers or the DMZ operator can see which datasets are requested, when, and by whom.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for identifiability/inference from observable access requests and dataset selection.

title: Insufficient proof of who retrieved which research data and when
description: If retrieval events are not strongly bound to the authenticated recipient and integrity-protected, the recipient could deny having retrieved specific data, or the sender could be unable to prove what was made available and accessed.
assumptions: Auditability is important for governed research data release and current logging may be incomplete, mutable, or not recipient-bound.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation gaps in data access/retrieval events; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Overbroad data publication in the DMZ discloses more data than necessary
description: Making a dataset available in the DMZ may expose attributes or records beyond what is context-relevant for the Trusted Research Data Recipient, violating data minimization and increasing privacy impact if retrieved or browsed.
assumptions: Dataset preparation or export to the DMZ may include excess fields, records, or metadata beyond the approved sharing scope.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for excessive disclosure / not data-minimized release.

title: Recipient can infer sensitive information from metadata or aggregate characteristics of the delivered data
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, the delivered dataset, filenames, schema, counts, timestamps, or contextual metadata may enable deduction of sensitive attributes, cohort membership, or other confidential facts about individuals.
assumptions: The shared data or its accompanying metadata is pseudonymized, aggregated, or otherwise transformed rather than fully anonymous.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for deductive disclosure via inference from dataset contents or metadata; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Data made available without adequate consent, legal basis, or sharing constraints enforcement
description: The DMZ may make research data available for retrieval in a way that exceeds the data subjects' consent, ethical approval, data use agreement, or other legal/governance constraints applicable to the recipient and purpose.
assumptions: This flow is governed by consent, ethics, contract, or regulatory restrictions that must be enforced at release time.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for non-compliance due to unlawful or policy-violating disclosure.

title: Data subjects are not informed that their data is being made available to an external recipient
description: Making context-relevant research data available via the DMZ to an external trusted recipient may occur without sufficient transparency to data subjects about the recipient, purpose, timing, or scope of sharing.
assumptions: Transparency notices may be incomplete, generic, or not updated for this specific downstream disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency around external data sharing.

title: Published research data may enable linkage across datasets
description: Context-relevant research data made available in the NCCoE-managed publishing location may contain stable identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or unique combinations of attributes that allow recipients to link records to other datasets and infer the same data subject across contexts.
assumptions: The published data is accessible to multiple trusted parties and may include direct or indirect identifiers or metadata sufficient for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on linkage via identifiers/quasi-identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Published dataset may reveal identities of research subjects
description: If the research data or associated metadata includes direct identifiers, pseudonyms, rare attributes, or small-cell statistics, authorized recipients retrieving it from the publishing location may be able to identify individual data subjects.
assumptions: The dataset is not fully anonymized and may preserve attributes that permit singling out or re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability/re-identification from released data.

title: Publication may disclose sensitive personal information beyond intended audience expectations
description: Making context-relevant research data available for retrieval can disclose sensitive facts about individuals to a broader set of trusted interested parties than necessary, especially where access scope, downstream use, or dataset contents are not tightly minimized.
assumptions: The research data contains personal or sensitive attributes and the recipient community is larger than the minimum necessary set.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure from data release; exact subtree label may differ.

title: Publishing location may expose detectability of a subject's inclusion in the dataset
description: Even if the content is partly protected, the presence of records, filenames, metadata, timestamps, or access patterns in the publishing location may allow an observer or authorized user to detect whether a particular individual or study participant is included in the published research data.
assumptions: Metadata, dataset naming, indexing, or query/access behavior is observable to some users of the publishing location.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability of data/subject presence from metadata or access characteristics.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their research data is being published for retrieval by trusted parties
description: Individuals whose data appears in the context-relevant research dataset may not understand that their information will be placed in an NCCoE-managed publishing location for access by researchers and other trusted interested parties, reducing transparency about processing and sharing.
assumptions: Notices, consent materials, or other transparency mechanisms may not clearly describe this publication and retrieval use case.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient transparency/awareness; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Publication and access sharing may exceed consent, authorization, or legal basis
description: Making the research data available in the publishing location to trusted interested parties may go beyond the purposes, consent terms, data sharing agreements, or other legal basis under which the data was originally collected or provided.
assumptions: Use restrictions, consent limitations, or sharing agreements may not fully cover publication for this audience and purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with consent/purpose limitation/legal basis; exact subtree label may vary.

title: Sender may later deny having submitted or authorized publication of the dataset
description: If the upload or transfer from the trusted data recipient to the NCCoE-managed publishing location is not strongly logged and attributable, the sender could dispute having submitted a particular version of the research data or authorized its publication, complicating accountability for privacy-relevant disclosures.
assumptions: Submission logging, approval workflows, or provenance controls may be incomplete or weak.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation of data submission/publication actions; exact node id may differ.

title: Publicly accessible published research data may disclose personal or sensitive information
description: Making context-relevant research data available from an externally managed publishing location can expose personal data, quasi-identifiers, or sensitive attributes to any researcher or interested party who can retrieve it. If the dataset is insufficiently minimized, anonymized, or aggregated, individuals represented in the data may be directly or indirectly identified from the published content.
assumptions: The published research data may include personal data, special-category data, or combinations of attributes that can relate to individuals.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for content/data disclosure due to publication; exact LINDDUN Pro node mapping may vary.

title: Published dataset may enable re-identification through linkage
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed before publication, releasing context-relevant research data through a public or broadly accessible location can allow recipients to link records with external datasets and re-identify individuals. The publication location increases the audience and availability for such correlation attacks.
assumptions: The dataset contains indirect identifiers or unique combinations of values and external auxiliary datasets are available.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability via data linkage/re-identification.

title: Accesses to the publishing location may allow linkability of requester behavior
description: Researchers and interested parties retrieving the published data from the externally managed location may have their requests, IP addresses, account identifiers, or download patterns logged. Those logs can allow the operator or other parties with log access to link multiple retrieval events to the same person or organization over time.
assumptions: The externally managed publishing location logs requests or uses persistent identifiers such as accounts, cookies, or stable network metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of multiple accesses/transactions; exact tree node may differ.

title: Metadata and access logs at the publishing location may disclose who retrieved the data
description: Because the data is hosted at an externally managed publishing location, the hosting party may collect and retain access metadata such as identities, IP addresses, timestamps, user agents, and referrers. Disclosure of these logs can reveal who was interested in or obtained the research data, creating a privacy risk for requesters as well as for any data subjects implied by access patterns.
assumptions: The publishing location maintains operational or analytics logs and those logs are accessible to administrators, third parties, or through compromise/legal process.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of request/usage metadata rather than dataset content itself.

title: Publisher may be unable to prove what version of data was made available
description: If the transfer from the trusted data recipient to the externally managed publishing location lacks robust audit trails, timestamps, or integrity-protected publication records, the sender may later be unable to demonstrate exactly which dataset version was published, when it was released, or under what permissions. This can undermine accountability for privacy-relevant publication decisions.
assumptions: Publication events are not immutably logged or signed, and dataset versioning/provenance controls are weak.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is less central than disclosure here; node id is an approximate best fit.

title: Publication may exceed the data subjects' consent or expected use
description: Making research data available for retrieval by researchers and interested parties may be incompatible with the purposes, audience, retention, or dissemination scope originally communicated to data subjects. If publication occurs without a matching legal basis, consent scope, or other authorization, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The data originated from individuals under purpose, consent, contractual, ethical, or regulatory constraints that may not permit broad publication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unlawful/unsupported processing or purpose expansion; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that their data is being published externally
description: If the research data is made available through an externally managed publishing location without clear notice, data subjects may not understand that their information, or information derived from them, is being disseminated to a wider audience. This reduces transparency about where the data is stored, who can access it, and for what purposes.
assumptions: Notices are incomplete, difficult to access, or do not specifically mention external publication and retrieval by third parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/awareness; exact node id may differ.

title: Sensitive outreach message may disclose existence of a new health-related record
description: If the outreach attempt explicitly states that a new record was added to the patient's file, anyone who can see or hear the message (shared phone, voicemail, SMS preview, email preview, postal mail opened by others) may learn sensitive information about the patient and the existence of an interaction or enrollment event.
assumptions: The content of the outreach contains enough detail to reveal that a record exists and may relate to healthcare, enrollment, or another sensitive context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure via message content; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Outreach channel metadata can identify the patient and link them to the previous enrollment entity
description: Even when message content is minimal, call logs, SMS headers, email metadata, envelope information, or caller identification can reveal that the patient is being contacted by the previous enrollment entity, enabling identification and linkage between the patient and that organization or program.
assumptions: The outreach uses a channel that exposes sender/recipient metadata to telecom providers, device users, household members, or other observers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability through communication metadata.

title: Patient may be unable to determine whether the outreach is legitimate or phishing
description: If the patient cannot authenticate that the outreach genuinely originated from the previous enrollment entity, they may be deceived into disclosing personal information or acting on a fraudulent message. Lack of sender authenticity also undermines trust in privacy notices or requests for follow-up.
assumptions: The communication channel does not provide strong, user-verifiable authenticity signals, or the patient is not able to verify them.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for sender authenticity / detectability of deception; exact subtree may differ.

title: No reliable proof of notification delivery or content
description: The third party may later be unable to prove what notification was sent, when it was sent, and whether it reached the patient. Conversely, the patient may be unable to prove that an unexpected disclosure occurred. This can hinder dispute resolution around improper outreach or consent boundaries.
assumptions: The outreach process lacks auditable logging, delivery receipts, or preserved message records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation relating to sending/receiving a notification.

title: Outreach may occur without appropriate consent, legal basis, or channel preference
description: Informing the patient about a new record may violate privacy expectations or regulatory requirements if the patient did not consent to be contacted by this entity, withdrew consent, or restricted contact methods. Use of insecure or disallowed channels can also create non-compliance risks.
assumptions: Applicable laws, contractual terms, or patient preferences constrain whether and how outreach may occur.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of consent/legal basis or policy non-compliance; exact subtree may vary.

title: Repeated outreach attempts can make the patient linkable across contexts
description: Multiple notifications over time, especially using stable identifiers such as phone number, email address, or mailing address, can allow observers or service providers to correlate contacts and link the patient to repeated enrollment or record-management events.
assumptions: The same identifiers or channels are reused across outreach attempts and are observable by third parties or shared-device users.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via repeated communications and stable identifiers.

title: Job submissions can reveal the bioinformaticist's identity or role
description: Tool-selection and job-queue requests may contain direct identifiers, account names, lab affiliations, project identifiers, or distinctive command patterns that allow the Compute Nodes or associated operators to identify which bioinformaticist submitted a job.
assumptions: Assumes job requests or scheduler metadata include user/account identifiers or are observable by platform operators or other components.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for identifiability via explicit or implicit identifiers in submitted requests.

title: Repeated job-queue activity can be linked to the same bioinformaticist
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, recurring submission timing, preferred tools, parameter templates, queue destinations, and project-specific workflows can allow observers to link multiple job submissions to the same person or team over time.
assumptions: Assumes logs, scheduler telemetry, or operational staff can observe repeated submission patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for linkability caused by repeated observable patterns across submissions.

title: Tool choices and job parameters may disclose sensitive research intent
description: The selected bioinformatics tools, reference datasets, pipelines, and scheduler parameters can reveal sensitive information about the underlying sequence data, disease focus, cohort type, or research hypothesis, even if the raw sequence data is not in this flow.
assumptions: Assumes the job request includes tool names, workflow definitions, parameters, dataset references, or resource requirements that correlate with sensitive study context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-fit estimate for disclosure of information contained in message content/metadata.

title: Queue metadata and execution feedback may expose sensitive operational details
description: Compute Nodes may generate acknowledgements, queue records, scheduling metadata, or status traces derived from the submission that expose project names, sample identifiers, or tool-specific details to unauthorized internal viewers.
assumptions: Assumes submission details are logged or surfaced in scheduler/cluster monitoring accessible beyond strictly authorized personnel.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure through derived records/metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of submission can enable repudiation of queued jobs
description: If job-queue requests are not strongly authenticated, integrity-protected, and audit-logged, a bioinformaticist could later deny having selected a specific tool or submitted a particular analysis job, complicating accountability and incident investigation.
assumptions: Assumes weak submission logging, shared accounts, or lack of tamper-evident audit trails.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation of an action; exact node id may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Bioinformaticist may be unaware of secondary use of submission metadata
description: The user may not understand that tool-selection choices, command parameters, and queue timing are collected in logs and may be used for monitoring, performance analytics, productivity assessment, or other secondary purposes beyond job execution.
assumptions: Assumes notice and transparency around scheduler logging and downstream use of operational metadata are incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for lack of awareness/transparency regarding data handling.

title: Job-submission metadata may be processed without an adequate privacy basis or minimization
description: The platform may collect and retain more submission metadata than necessary—such as persistent user identifiers, detailed command lines, project labels, or sample references—without sufficient purpose limitation, minimization, or retention controls.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policy or regulatory obligations require minimization, purpose limitation, retention limits, or access controls for operational metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ depending on the compliance obligation in scope.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of final clinical report to the bioinformaticist
description: The Clinical Result Generation App may expose the final clinical report, which can contain highly sensitive health and genetic information, to a bioinformaticist who is not authorized to access the full finalized report or all of its contents.
assumptions: Assumes role-based access controls may be insufficiently scoped, and that the bioinformaticist does not always have a need-to-know for the complete final report.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-fit estimate for information disclosure via unauthorized access; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Overexposure of report contents beyond minimum necessary
description: The app may provide the entire final clinical report, including identifiers, incidental findings, or clinician-oriented commentary, when the bioinformaticist only needs a subset. This increases privacy exposure of patient data.
assumptions: Assumes the report includes more personal data than is strictly necessary for the bioinformaticist's task.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture excessive data disclosure / lack of data minimization in the disclosed report.

title: Linkability of final report to other genomic or clinical records
description: By retrieving the final clinical report, the bioinformaticist can link report contents, identifiers, case numbers, or genomic findings with other internal datasets, increasing the ability to correlate records belonging to the same patient across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes common identifiers or quasi-identifiers are present in the report and accessible to the bioinformaticist.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through shared identifiers in disclosed data; exact subnode may vary.

title: Interception of final clinical report during retrieval
description: If the report is pulled over an insufficiently protected channel or via insecure client configuration, sensitive report data could be intercepted in transit between the app and the bioinformaticist.
assumptions: Assumes transport security, endpoint validation, or session protection could be misconfigured or absent.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for disclosure in transit/eavesdropping.

title: Unnecessary identifiability of the patient in the final report
description: The final clinical report may include direct identifiers such as name, MRN, date of birth, or other identifying details, making the patient directly identifiable to the bioinformaticist when this may not be necessary for the task.
assumptions: Assumes some workflow variants do not require the bioinformaticist to see direct patient identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability caused by included direct identifiers; exact subnode uncertain.

title: Insufficient proof or logging of report access
description: If the Clinical Result Generation App does not create reliable audit logs for report retrieval, the bioinformaticist could later deny having accessed a specific patient's final report, weakening accountability for privacy-relevant access.
assumptions: Assumes logging, user binding, or tamper resistance may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node for lack of non-repudiation/accountable access logging.

title: Bioinformaticist may be unaware of secondary use or sensitivity constraints on final reports
description: The app may not clearly communicate sensitivity labels, permitted use, retention constraints, or downstream sharing restrictions associated with the final clinical report, leading to privacy-harming handling by the recipient.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not adequately present purpose limitation or handling obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit estimate for unawareness due to missing privacy notices or contextual cues.

title: Retrieval of final clinical report without enforcing consent or purpose restrictions
description: The app may allow the bioinformaticist to pull the final clinical report even when patient consent, role restrictions, or purpose limitation do not permit this access, creating a compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes access decisions should depend on consent, legal basis, or workflow purpose, and these may not be technically enforced.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node for non-compliance with consent, purpose limitation, or access-policy obligations.

title: Linkability of genetics-related recommendations across patient records and contexts
description: Professional recommendations and clinical next steps derived from genetic care are stored in the External EMR. If these entries are associated with stable patient, clinician, encounter, or case identifiers, they can be linked with other EMR data and potentially with research-related datasets, enabling correlation of sensitive genetics-related context across visits or systems.
assumptions: The External EMR stores persistent identifiers and allows later retrieval or integration with other clinical/research records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Identifiability of the patient from stored genetics-related clinical notes
description: The recommendations and next steps entered into the External EMR may directly identify the patient through names, record numbers, dates, or indirectly through rare genetic findings, family history context, or unique care pathways. This can make the patient identifiable even if the data is treated as context-relevant research data.
assumptions: The logged information may include direct identifiers or sufficiently specific quasi-identifiers/clinical details.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate; exact Pro tree mapping may be more specific.

title: Disclosure of sensitive genetic and clinical inference information in the EMR
description: Storing genetic physician recommendations in an external EMR can expose sensitive information about suspected or confirmed genetic conditions, reproductive risk, family implications, or recommended interventions to parties who can access the EMR beyond the minimum necessary audience.
assumptions: The External EMR is accessible by multiple roles, organizations, or integrated services beyond the genetic physician alone.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subnode may differ.

title: Repudiation of having entered or authorized the genetics-related recommendation
description: If the flow lacks strong attribution, timestamps, or integrity-protected audit trails, the Genetic Physician could later deny having logged specific professional recommendations or clinical next steps, undermining accountability for processing sensitive patient information.
assumptions: Audit logging, non-repudiation controls, or strong author authentication may be absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate from memory.

title: Unawareness of secondary use or broad visibility of genetics-related entries
description: Patients may be unaware that genetics-related recommendations entered into the External EMR can be viewed by a broad set of care teams, retained for long periods, or reused for operational, research, or integration purposes beyond the immediate consultation context.
assumptions: Notice, consent, and transparency mechanisms around EMR storage and downstream use may be limited.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode uncertain; mapped to unawareness generally.

title: Non-compliance with data minimization and purpose limitation for genetics-related notes
description: The External EMR may store more genetics-related detail than is necessary for downstream care, or reuse the logged recommendations for purposes not aligned with the original clinical/research context, creating risk of non-compliance with privacy obligations such as minimization, purpose limitation, and special-category data handling.
assumptions: Genetic/research-context information may be especially regulated and may require stricter handling than standard clinical notes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact compliance subtree node may differ.

title: Sensitive genetic-related recommendations stored in EMR may expose highly personal information
description: The physician’s recommendations and clinical next steps, when recorded in the Internal EMR, can reveal genetic findings, suspected conditions, hereditary risks, or planned interventions. If the stored entry is accessible beyond those with a care or approved research need, the patient’s sensitive health and genetic context may be disclosed.
assumptions: The EMR entry contains context-rich narrative or coded data linked to an identifiable patient and may be accessible to multiple internal roles.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure from data at rest in the datastore; exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may differ.

title: Research-related clinical notes in the EMR may enable linkage across care and research contexts
description: Storing context-relevant research data together with routine clinical records can allow recipients of the EMR data to link a patient’s research participation, genetic context, and clinical pathway. This can increase the ability to correlate records across systems or contexts that were expected to remain separated.
assumptions: The recorded recommendation is associated with a patient identifier and may be combined with other clinical or research datasets.
uncertainty_note: I am confident about linkability risk, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id may be a different L.1.x subtype.

title: EMR entry may allow inference of undisclosed genetic status or family risk
description: Even if the note does not explicitly state a diagnosis, professional recommendations and next steps can imply the presence of a genetic variant, elevated hereditary risk, or likely future treatment path. Observers could infer sensitive facts about the patient, and potentially relatives, from the content or metadata of the stored recommendation.
assumptions: Clinical recommendations are specific enough that a knowledgeable party could infer underlying genetic conclusions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit inference node; exact subtype may vary depending on whether inference is from content, metadata, or associated workflow state.

title: The patient may be unaware that research-context recommendations are recorded in the internal EMR
description: If recommendations derived from a research context are entered into the Internal EMR without clear notice, the patient may not understand that this information is being stored in the clinical record, potentially used by other clinicians, or retained under different governance than the research system.
assumptions: There may be insufficient transparency to the patient about migration of research-context information into the clinical EMR.
uncertainty_note: This is a transparency/unawareness concern; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro depending on whether the focus is collection, storage, or sharing notice.

title: Recording research-context genetic recommendations in the EMR may exceed consent or legal basis
description: If the professional recommendations and next steps originate from research activity, copying them into the Internal EMR may be incompatible with the patient’s consent, original purpose limitation, or applicable rules for use of genetic and research data. This creates a risk that processing in the EMR is not compliant with applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: The data originated in or is materially influenced by a research context and may be subject to special consent, governance, or jurisdiction-specific protections.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance clearly applies as a possibility, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id may map to a more specific purpose-limitation or consent-related subtype.

title: Insufficient proof of what recommendation the physician actually submitted
description: If the flow from the Genetic Physician to the Internal EMR lacks strong attribution, integrity protection, or auditability, the physician could later dispute having entered a specific recommendation or clinical next step, and the organization may be unable to reliably prove the origin and timing of the entry.
assumptions: The flow may rely on ordinary application logging without strong non-repudiation controls such as robust audit trails or signed submissions.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is less central to privacy than disclosure/inference here; node id is a best-fit high-level mapping.

title: Unauthorized retrieval of retained physical samples from storage
description: A remainder physical sample stored after contextual retention requirements are met could be retrieved by personnel who are not authorized to access that sample. This would disclose the existence of a sample and potentially sensitive information associated with the individual from whom it originated.
assumptions: Physical sample storage contains identifiable or linkable samples and access is not perfectly restricted or monitored.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized access/disclosure from a data store; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for physical sample storage may vary.

title: Sample remainder can be linked back to the data subject
description: Even after the contextual retention milestone is reached, the stored remainder sample may retain direct labels, coded identifiers, or chain-of-custody references that allow the sample to be linked to a specific person or case. This enables association of the physical sample with that individual's records or prior interactions.
assumptions: The sample or its container carries identifiers or is stored with metadata that can be cross-referenced.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability/linkability of a stored artifact; exact subtree naming may differ.

title: Stored sample enables linkage across contexts or datasets
description: The retained remainder sample may be correlated with other specimens, laboratory records, or research datasets using common identifiers, barcodes, storage location metadata, or distinctive sample characteristics. This could reveal relationships between records that were expected to remain separate.
assumptions: Common identifiers or stable quasi-identifiers are shared across systems or storage processes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkage node id; exact LINDDUN Pro linkage subtree may differ.

title: Retention or retrieval of sample remainder may exceed stated purpose or legal basis
description: Retrieving and continuing to store the remainder physical sample after contextual retention requirements have been met may be inconsistent with the original purpose limitation, retention schedule, or consent/legal basis governing the sample. This creates a risk of non-compliance with privacy obligations.
assumptions: There are explicit retention, purpose-limitation, or consent constraints applicable to the sample lifecycle.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id for over-retention or use beyond allowed purpose; exact subtree may differ.

title: Technician can repudiate having retrieved or returned the physical sample
description: If retrieval and return-to-storage actions are not logged with sufficient detail, the technician may later deny having handled the remainder sample. This undermines accountability for who accessed the sample, when, and for what purpose.
assumptions: Audit logs, signatures, or chain-of-custody controls may be incomplete for manual physical handling steps.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of accountability/non-repudiation in a physical handling process; exact subtree may differ.

title: Individuals may be unaware that remainder samples are retrieved and retained in storage
description: The data subject may not be adequately informed that the remainder of a physical sample will be retrieved and kept in storage after immediate contextual needs have been satisfied, including how long it will be retained and for what downstream uses. This reduces transparency and informed expectations.
assumptions: Notices, consent materials, or operational transparency about sample retention are incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Disposed sample remnants may still disclose personal or sensitive information
description: If the physical sample is not irreversibly destroyed or is placed into a disposal store/container that can be accessed, inspected, or recovered, remaining material may reveal information about the data subject (e.g., health, genetic, or other biological characteristics). Disposal therefore creates a risk of information disclosure from residual sample material.
assumptions: The disposal item/store may temporarily hold sample material before final destruction, and unauthorized parties could gain physical access to it.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode for disclosure via improper disposal of physical media may differ.

title: Sample disposal container or records may allow identification of the sample donor
description: Labels, identifiers, chain-of-custody markers, or linked disposal records associated with the disposed physical sample may enable someone with access to the disposal item to identify the individual from whom the sample originated.
assumptions: Disposed samples or their associated disposal records retain direct identifiers, pseudonyms, barcodes, or references that can be linked back to a person.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from stored/disposed sample artifacts; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Disposed sample artifacts may be linkable across contexts or systems
description: Persistent sample IDs, barcodes, or disposal-log references can allow an observer to link the disposed sample to other laboratory, clinical, or research records, revealing that records in different contexts relate to the same individual or specimen.
assumptions: A stable identifier or consistent metadata is retained on the sample, container, or disposal records and is also present in other systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability through persistent identifiers on disposal artifacts; exact subnode may differ.

title: Sample disposal action may be insufficiently provable
description: If there is no reliable, tamper-evident logging or witnessed confirmation of destruction/disposal, the technician or organization may later be unable to prove that the sample remainder was actually disposed of when retention requirements were met.
assumptions: The process relies on manual handling and may lack signed, audited, or tamper-evident disposal records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of evidence/non-repudiation around disposal events; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Disposal may occur in a way that is incompatible with retention, consent, or policy constraints
description: If the technician disposes of the physical sample without correctly verifying applicable retention schedules, consent terms, legal holds, or study-specific policies, the disposal operation may violate compliance obligations related to personal data handling.
assumptions: Retention and disposal rules differ across sample types, jurisdictions, or study protocols, and enforcement is partly manual.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for policy/consent non-compliance in disposal processing; exact subnode may differ.

title: Residual biological material on reused flow cell can disclose genetic information
description: If a used flow cell is not thoroughly cleaned, residual physical sample material may remain and be accessible during later handling or reuse. That residue could enable disclosure of sensitive biological or genetic information from the previous sample subject to unauthorized parties or subsequent users/processes.
assumptions: Assumes flow cells may be handled, inspected, or reused after a sequencing run and that residual material can still reveal sample-associated information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected from general information disclosure concepts; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for physical residual data disclosure may vary.

title: Residual sample remnants on flow cell may link sequencing runs or data subjects
description: Remaining sample traces on a reused flow cell could allow an observer or downstream process to associate a prior sequencing run with a later run, linking data subjects, samples, or experiments that should remain separate.
assumptions: Assumes enough residual material or metadata/context exists to correlate one run or sample with another when the same flow cell is reused.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a linkage threat arising from physical sample carryover rather than a canonical digital identifier.

title: Residual material on flow cell may enable identification of a prior sample subject
description: Biological residue left on the used flow cell may permit identification of the individual or source associated with the prior sample, especially where genetic material is uniquely identifying.
assumptions: Assumes residual sample quantity/quality is sufficient for identification and that an attacker or unauthorized processor can access it.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; identification here stems from leftover biological material rather than explicit identifiers in a digital flow.

title: Insufficient cleaning/disposal practice for used flow cells may violate data minimization and storage limitation obligations
description: Failure by the technician to clean or otherwise safely dispose of used flow cells can retain unnecessary physical sample remnants beyond the intended sequencing purpose, creating non-compliance with privacy requirements for secure deletion, minimization, or purpose limitation.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policy, contractual, or regulatory obligations require effective removal or secure disposal of residual sample material.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate because this maps a physical sanitization failure to a generic non-compliance category.

title: Linkability of transformed research datasets stored in the cluster filesystem
description: Context-relevant research data derived from raw sequence data may retain stable identifiers, pseudonyms, sample IDs, genomic signatures, or consistent metadata that allow records in the cluster filesystem to be linked back to other datasets or processing runs concerning the same individual or cohort.
assumptions: The stored outputs preserve some persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or high-dimensional genomic features across datasets or runs.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for dataset/linkage via stored identifiers and attributes; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Identifiability of individuals from stored context-relevant research data
description: Even after transformation, context-relevant research data derived from sequence data can remain inherently identifying or become identifying when combined with metadata, because genomic and research-context attributes may point to a unique person or small group.
assumptions: The derived dataset contains genomic features, rare variants, phenotype/context fields, or metadata sufficient to single out a data subject.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for direct/indirect identifiability in stored data; exact subnode id may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive information through persisted derived data
description: The cluster filesystem stores derived research data that may reveal sensitive health, ancestry, familial, or other research-related information. Unauthorized access, broad internal sharing, or weak segregation on the filesystem could expose these sensitive inferences.
assumptions: Stored outputs are accessible to multiple jobs, users, or administrators and include sensitive attributes or inferences.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure from stored sensitive data; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Detectability of a subject's presence via filesystem artifacts
description: The act of writing context-relevant research data to the cluster filesystem may create observable files, paths, timestamps, job outputs, or access patterns that allow an observer to detect that a particular sample, study, or subject is being processed or included, even without reading the file contents.
assumptions: Other tenants, operators, or monitoring systems can observe filenames, directory structures, timestamps, file sizes, or access events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability from metadata/side channels around data storage; exact subnode id may differ.

title: Processing and storage of derived research data beyond consent or permitted purpose
description: Raw sequence data is transformed into context-relevant research data and stored for research use. This may exceed the original consent, governance approval, retention limit, or allowed purpose if derivation, enrichment, or persistence is broader than what data subjects were informed about or authorized.
assumptions: Consent, ethics approval, data-use agreements, or retention policies may constrain derivation, enrichment, sharing, or storage duration.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with consent/purpose/retention obligations; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Unauthorized access to uploaded final clinical reports on the 3rd Party Portal
description: The final clinical report likely contains sensitive personal and health information. If access controls on the 3rd Party Portal are weak, misconfigured, or overly broad, unauthorized parties may view or retrieve the uploaded report, disclosing patient information.
assumptions: Assumes the final clinical report contains personal data and is accessible through the portal after upload.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for unauthorized data access/disclosure at the receiving data store, but exact LINDDUN Pro node labeling may vary.

title: Interception or exposure of the final clinical report during upload to the portal
description: If the upload channel between the Bioinformaticist and the 3rd Party Portal lacks adequate transport protection or is improperly configured, the report may be exposed to network attackers or intermediaries during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the flow traverses a network and transport/session protections may be relevant.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for data disclosure in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may differ.

title: Portal can identify the patient from the final clinical report
description: The uploaded final clinical report may directly identify the patient through names, identifiers, dates, or other clinical details, allowing the 3rd Party Portal operator or recipients to identify a natural person.
assumptions: Assumes the report contains direct or indirect patient identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node; exact sub-node may differ depending on whether direct or indirect identifiers dominate.

title: Linkability of the clinical report with other portal-held records
description: Data in the uploaded final clinical report may be linked with other reports, account records, case identifiers, or external datasets held by the 3rd Party Portal, enabling correlation of activities and records concerning the same patient.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores multiple related records or has access to auxiliary datasets.
uncertainty_note: Approximate best-fit node for linkability via shared identifiers or report metadata.

title: Insufficient proof of report upload or receipt
description: If the portal does not maintain trustworthy audit logs, timestamps, or acknowledgements, the Bioinformaticist or the portal may later dispute whether the final clinical report was uploaded, received, or altered, undermining accountability for personal-data handling.
assumptions: Assumes auditability and upload confirmation are not guaranteed by design.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit approximation for lack of non-repudiation of data submission/receipt.

title: Uploading the final clinical report to the 3rd Party Portal may exceed the patient's consent or stated purpose
description: The final clinical report may be transferred to a 3rd Party Portal for purposes, recipients, retention periods, or jurisdictions not covered by the patient's consent, notice, or other legal basis, creating non-compliance with privacy requirements.
assumptions: Assumes consent, notice, contractual, or regulatory restrictions may apply to sharing clinical reports with third parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact sub-node depends on the applicable legal basis and policy constraints.

title: Patient may be unaware that the final clinical report is uploaded to a 3rd Party Portal
description: If the use of the 3rd Party Portal is not transparent to the patient, the patient may not understand who receives the report, where it is stored, or how it is further processed, limiting meaningful awareness and control.
assumptions: Assumes patient-facing notices do not clearly explain this transfer.
uncertainty_note: Approximate best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency regarding downstream disclosure.

title: Residual copies or metadata of the uploaded report may be exposed on the portal
description: Beyond the report content itself, thumbnails, previews, filenames, version history, caches, backup copies, or metadata generated by the portal may disclose sensitive patient or case information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the portal generates derivative artifacts or stores metadata about uploaded files.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for disclosure via derived artifacts/metadata at the data store.

title: Overexposure of sensitive report contents to portal operators or unauthorized internal viewers
description: The final clinical report contains highly sensitive genetic and clinical information. While stored and made available for download in the 3rd Party Portal, personnel operating the portal or other unauthorized parties with backend or administrative access may be able to view the report contents beyond what is necessary for delivery to the Genetic Counselor.
assumptions: The portal stores or renders the report in a way that may be accessible to administrators, support staff, or compromised internal accounts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary depending on whether the portal exposes content via storage access, admin interfaces, or transmission paths.

title: Ability to infer patient identity or case linkage from downloaded report metadata
description: Even if the transfer is intended only for the Genetic Counselor, the downloaded final clinical report and its surrounding metadata (patient name, identifiers, accession numbers, timestamps, clinician references, rare-condition details) can allow direct identification of the patient or strong linkage of the report to a specific individual or case.
assumptions: The report includes direct identifiers or quasi-identifiers, and the counselor's endpoint or workflow exposes filenames, notifications, download history, or local storage metadata.
uncertainty_note: Inference here is used in the LINDDUN sense of deriving identity from available data; node id is a best-fit high-level choice.

title: Insufficient proof of report access or download by the Genetic Counselor
description: If the portal does not create reliable, tamper-resistant audit records for report download and access events, the Genetic Counselor could later deny having accessed the final clinical report, or the organization may be unable to demonstrate who accessed it and when.
assumptions: Access logging may be incomplete, mutable, or not strongly bound to an authenticated individual session.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-repudiation subnode may differ depending on whether the emphasis is on sender, receiver, or evidence quality.

title: Genetic Counselor may be unaware of portal-side retention, logging, or onward sharing of report access data
description: During report download, the Genetic Counselor may not have sufficient visibility into how the 3rd Party Portal logs the access, retains downloaded-report metadata, or shares operational data with third parties. This lack of transparency can undermine informed expectations around privacy handling for this sensitive report.
assumptions: The portal provider collects access logs, telemetry, or support data that are not clearly communicated to users.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is applied to the receiving user of the portal; some analyses may instead model this at system-level notice/consent artifacts rather than directly on the flow.

title: Download and handling of the final clinical report may not comply with data-minimization, access-control, or retention obligations
description: Providing the full final clinical report through the 3rd Party Portal may exceed what is necessary if broader report content, longer-than-needed availability, or insufficient access restrictions are used. This can create non-compliance with privacy, confidentiality, retention, or purpose-limitation requirements for genetic health data.
assumptions: Applicable legal, contractual, or organizational rules impose strict controls on access scope, retention, and disclosure of genetic reports.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit compliance node only; exact subnode depends on the governing obligation (e.g., minimization, retention, lawful access control, cross-border handling).

title: Report download may reveal the counselor's involvement in a specific patient case
description: Observing that the Genetic Counselor downloads a particular final clinical report can reveal that this counselor is assigned to, or involved in, a specific patient case or condition. Access logs, network monitoring, filenames, and portal activity traces may disclose this association to unauthorized observers.
assumptions: Download events or report references are visible in logs, notifications, endpoint artifacts, or network metadata to parties beyond those with a need to know.
uncertainty_note: Detectability/disclosure distinction can overlap here; this is modeled as detectability of the counselor-case association from observable download activity.

title: Disclosure of context-relevant research/genetic data to an unintended clinician or unauthorized recipient
description: The genetic counselor makes context-relevant clinical/research data available for retrieval by the clinician with added input and analysis. If access control, recipient selection, or transmission protection is weak, sensitive genetic and related clinical information could be disclosed to someone other than the intended clinician.
assumptions: The flow contains sensitive patient-linked genetic or clinical research information and is retrievable through some shared system or channel.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN knowledge; exact Pro subtree may vary.

title: Identifiability of the patient from shared context-relevant research/genetic data
description: Even if the shared dataset is intended to be context-relevant only, the combination of genetic findings, clinical context, and additional clinician input may directly or indirectly identify the patient.
assumptions: The data includes patient-specific genetic variants, rare-disease context, or detailed clinical attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit; identifiability may also overlap with linkability/disclosure depending on implementation.

title: Linkability of this research/genetic data with other patient records
description: The clinician may combine the received context-relevant research/genetic data with local EHR data, prior cases, or external datasets, enabling linkage across contexts and revealing a more complete patient profile than intended.
assumptions: The clinician has access to other identifiable or pseudonymous patient datasets that share attributes with this flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit approximate node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Unawareness by the patient regarding secondary clinical/research use and retrieval of their data
description: The patient may be unaware that the genetic counselor is making context-relevant research/clinical data available for clinician retrieval, additional input, and analysis, particularly if this extends beyond the patient's expected care interaction.
assumptions: Patient notices/consent materials may not clearly explain this sharing and analysis step.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; mapped to unawareness concerning processing and sharing transparency.

title: Non-compliance with consent, purpose limitation, or data-minimization obligations
description: Making research-related genetic/clinical data available to the clinician could exceed the scope of the patient's consent, the original research purpose, or minimum-necessary sharing obligations if more data than needed is exposed for retrieval and analysis.
assumptions: Applicable legal, ethical, or organizational rules constrain reuse of research/genetic data for clinical retrieval and analysis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from general knowledge; exact Pro node may differ by whether the issue is consent, purpose limitation, or minimization.

title: Lack of evidence of receipt, access, or subsequent use of the shared data
description: If retrieval and later clinician input/analysis are not logged or attributable, parties may be unable to prove who accessed the context-relevant research/genetic data, when it was used, or what downstream disclosures occurred.
assumptions: The system/channel supporting retrieval may have incomplete audit logging or weak user attribution.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; non-repudiation mapping depends on available accountability controls.

title: Residual genomic data remains recoverable on decommissioned devices
description: If wet lab devices are not securely wiped, sanitized, or destroyed before resale or disposal, residual digital genomic data and associated metadata may remain recoverable by subsequent owners or service personnel, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal data.
assumptions: The devices contain local storage, caches, logs, or removable media that may retain genomic or sample-related data after operational use.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via data remanence on a datastore; exact LINDDUN Pro node wording may differ.

title: Recoverable configuration, logs, or identifiers disclose patient or sample information
description: Even where primary datasets are removed, device logs, audit trails, file system metadata, job histories, network settings, user accounts, or cached exports may still reveal identifiers, sample IDs, operator names, or links to genomic processing activities, enabling disclosure of personal or sensitive information.
assumptions: The device stores operational metadata or logs that can be extracted during refurbishment, servicing, or resale.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture disclosure from metadata/log remnants rather than the main payload data.

title: No verifiable proof that decommissioning and sanitization were performed
description: If the decommissioning specialist does not create tamper-resistant records of sanitization steps, media destruction, or chain-of-custody, the organization may be unable to prove that privacy-preserving decommissioning actually occurred, undermining accountability and enabling repudiation after a leakage incident.
assumptions: The process relies on manual procedures or weak recordkeeping for device retirement and resale preparation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-repudiation node estimate for lack of evidence of an action; exact subtree identifier may differ.

title: Decommissioning does not meet privacy policy or legal retention/deletion obligations
description: Devices may be retired, resold, or disposed of without applying required privacy controls such as certified wiping, destruction of storage media, removal of accounts/keys, or documented disposal procedures, causing non-compliance with internal policy or applicable data protection obligations.
assumptions: There are defined privacy best practices, contractual requirements, or legal obligations governing deletion and secure disposal of genomic-data-processing equipment.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best-fit for non-compliance with deletion/disposal obligations in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Residual device identifiers and usage traces enable linkage to prior genomic processing activities
description: Persistent device identifiers, laboratory network settings, sample/job histories, and retained metadata on decommissioned devices could allow a recipient to link the device to specific laboratories, projects, samples, or data subjects, increasing the chance of correlating sensitive genomic information with other datasets.
assumptions: A downstream recipient can access retained identifiers or metadata and has auxiliary information about lab operations or prior device deployment.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the amount of retained metadata and attacker auxiliary knowledge; node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability through persistent identifiers/metadata.

title: Residual sensitive data on acquired/refurbished wet lab devices can be disclosed
description: Privacy-relevant wet lab devices acquired from third parties or refurbished may retain genomic or device-associated personal data from prior use. If sanitization is incomplete before the device becomes part of the environment, residual data could be accessible to the acquiring organization, service personnel, or later users, causing unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: The devices contain local storage, caches, logs, or embedded memory that may persist data from previous owners or servicing activities.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic disclosure node from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Acquired device provenance and refurbishment history may be insufficiently identifiable
description: If the organization cannot reliably identify the manufacturer source, refurbishment party, prior ownership state, or sanitization status of a device, it may be impossible to determine whether privacy-relevant data remains on the device or whether the device meets privacy requirements.
assumptions: Procurement and asset-management records may be incomplete or not cryptographically bound to the physical device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node from memory; exact node id may differ.

title: Supplier or refurbisher may repudiate sanitization or privacy-best-practice claims
description: A manufacturer, broker, or refurbisher could later deny having performed secure wiping, reconfiguration, or privacy-preserving refurbishment steps. Without evidence, the organization may be unable to prove compliance or assign responsibility after a disclosure incident.
assumptions: Sanitization/refurbishment attestations are not strongly logged, signed, or retained.
uncertainty_note: Exact repudiation node id is approximate.

title: Procurement of devices without verifiable privacy-preserving refurbishment may violate data minimization and storage limitation obligations
description: Introducing devices that still contain prior users' genomic or other personal data into the environment can amount to collecting or storing personal data without a valid purpose, lawful basis, or adequate safeguards, creating non-compliance with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Residual personal data from prior device use is present and accessible after acquisition.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance subtree id is a best estimate from memory.

title: Prior data subjects are unaware their data remains on transferred devices
description: Individuals whose genomic or related personal data was previously processed on the device may be unaware that their data persists after resale or refurbishment, preventing transparency and undermining their ability to exercise privacy rights.
assumptions: The device was previously used in contexts involving personal data and data remnants were not erased before transfer.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness node id is approximate.
